identity.name: Kahler-moduli-inflation nonthermal neutralino dark matter
identity.short_description: A nonthermal neutralino dark-matter scenario in fibred Calabi-Yau compactifications with Kahler moduli inflation and an MSSM-like D3-brane visible sector, where neutralinos are produced by inflaton/modulus decay and then undergo annihilation.
identity.historical_origin_or_motivation: The paper uses correlations among inflation, supersymmetry breaking, reheating, and dark-radiation production to select viable dark matter in string compactifications.

additional_dark_sector_particles: closed-string axions behaving as dark radiation
excited_or_degenerate_states: MSSM superpartners in the sequestered spectrum

mediator_types: MSSM electroweak bosons and Higgs bosons
annihilation_channels: neutralino pair annihilation after nonthermal production

theory.notes: The dark-matter candidate is an MSSM neutralino embedded in a string-inflation compactification with moduli reheating.

symmetries.stabilizing_mechanism: R-parity conservation is implicitly required for neutralino stability in the MSSM-like dark matter scenario.

mechanisms: nonthermal production from modulus/inflaton decay
post-decay neutralino annihilation
production.notes: The paper describes nonthermal dark matter after heavy-scalar decay and identifies an ultralocal KMI case where TeV-scale neutralinos are produced from inflaton decay and then annihilate.

nonstandard_features: early matter domination by a light modulus

phase_space.notes: Neutralinos are produced after reheating from scalar decay rather than as an ordinary thermal freeze-out population.

caveats: The paper emphasizes that the viable dark matter conclusion depends on UV correlations among inflation, supersymmetry breaking, reheating, and dark radiation.
validity_domain.notes: Do not apply to FI WIMP production, which the text says overproduces WIMPs.
